Text: The only bony joint between the upper limb and the axial skeleton is between the {{c1::clavicle}} and the {{c2::manubrium of the sternum}}.

Text: On a loose clavicle, the thick, blunt end with a triangular outline is the {{c1::sternal}} end; the broad, flattened end is the {{c1::acromial}} end.
Back Extra:
Why: the sternal end is built up to bear against the manubrium, while the acromial end flattens out to meet the small acromion.

Pitfall: 'flat' is used both ways: the lab's orientation rule and the instructor mean the sternal end's flat tip (like a nail head), but the manual means the acromial end's flattened shape, so go by thickness and call the thick end sternal.

Cue: the big bow you feel along your collarbone near the sternum is the forward curve.
